questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 6x + 8$ in rotations, evaluate $f(5)$.
Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 4$ and $x = 9$. Factoring $(x - 4)(x - 9) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 4$ and $x = 9$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 2x + 9$ in dilations, evaluate $f(2)$.
Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 1$ and $x = 3$. Factoring $(x - 1)(x - 3) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 1$ and $x = 3$.

questions.q: A data set recorded for dilations consists of the four values $\{12, 16, 20, 26\}$. What is the arithmetic mean? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $18.5$. The sum is $12 + 16 + 20 + 26 = 74$, and dividing by $4$ gives $18.5$.
questions.explanation: The sum is $12 + 16 + 20 + 26 = 74$, and dividing by $4$ gives $18.5$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 2x + 9$ in dilations, evaluate $f(3)$.
Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 2$ and $x = 4$. Factoring $(x - 2)(x - 4) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 2$ and $x = 4$.

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$ studying transformations, congruence, and similarity, $m\angle A = 51^\circ$ and $m\angle B = 45^\circ$. What is $m\angle C$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $84^\circ$. Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (51^\circ + 45^\circ) = 84^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (51^\circ + 45^\circ) = 84^\circ$.

questions.q: A geometric figure scaled by factor $k = 2$ has an original side length of $5\mathrm{\ cm}$. What is the corresponding image length? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $10\mathrm{\ cm}$. Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $5 \times 2 = 10\mathrm{\ cm}$.
questions.explanation: Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $5 \times 2 = 10\mathrm{\ cm}$.

questions.q: On the coordinate plane, a line with slope $m = 3$ passes through $(0, 3)$. What is its $y$-coordinate when $x = 1$? Show your complete algebraic work.
